title: Truth Table
definition: A truth table enumerates input truth combinations and the resulting value of a Boolean expression.
purpose: Make decision coverage, equivalence, and missing cases inspectable.
history: Truth tables provide a finite tabular method for defining and comparing propositional expressions.
mental_model: List every possible truth assignment, then calculate the expression one column at a time.
analogy: A complete test matrix covers every switch combination; the analogy fails when input domains have more than Boolean states.
common_mistakes: Calculating columns in the wrong order
industry_notes: Truth tables are practical for a small number of independent Boolean inputs; larger rule sets may need decision tables or model-based tests.
ai_notes: AI truth tables must be checked for 2^n rows, duplicate assignments, and correct intermediate columns.
interview_notes: Ask for all rows and an equivalence demonstration.
